dict.string: Every app iOS put on the Home screen except Safari and Settings.
Apps with no icon that the removed apps and services put on the screen: sign-in dialogs, share sheets, pickers and set-up screens.
The files iOS keeps to install a software update over the air. iOS 9.3.5 is the last version for this device.
The dictionaries and prediction data for typing in languages other than English, and the Japanese and Chinese input engine. English stays.
The stock wallpaper pictures, the moving wallpapers and the ringtones. The wallpaper in use is kept.
Files that only the removed apps and features used: the Music store's pages, the voice trigger data and the Apple Watch fonts.

The fonts for scripts other than Latin (Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic, Hebrew, the Indian scripts and others) and the display fonts the removed apps used. Pages in those scripts show empty boxes afterwards. The system font, the usual web fonts and emoji stay.

Data and frameworks that no program on the device links, opens or has read: the word-splitting data for Chinese, Japanese and Thai, raw camera support, the update progress pictures, and the OpenCL, voice trigger, slideshow and iWork preview frameworks.
The icons, road shields, styles and fonts Maps drew its maps with. The parts of the framework that location services read stay.
The voices that read text aloud in languages other than American English.
The models for recognising handwritten Chinese and other handwriting input.
The pictures the Photos app's editing effects were made from.
The alert tones of Messages, Mail, Calendar, the phone, payments, navigation and the Apple Watch. The keyboard, lock, power, screenshot and other system sounds stay.
The program that runs the cellular radio and its two launch definitions, which launchd does not load on a Wi-Fi iPad 2.
The wording of iOS in languages other than English, and the spelling dictionaries of those languages. Folders that take no space of their own are left.
Leftovers of iCloud and Online Services

Small programs, sign-in plug-ins, settings panels and lock screen plug-ins of iCloud, Apple ID, Find My iPad, Wallet, Mail, the social networks and the Apple Watch, which nothing on the device has used.
The services that look for updates to iOS and to its time zone data, and that gather and send usage and diagnostic reports to Apple. Crash reports are still written.

The services behind iMessage, FaceTime, call history and the blocked callers list. The identity service they share stays, because Wi-Fi, location and the Home screen ask for it without pause when it is gone.
The services behind iCloud, Find My iPad, Family Sharing, Apple ID sign-in, iCloud backup and Apple's push notifications.

The services behind the App Store, iTunes Store, Music, Game Center, Home, Health, Maps, Tips, iTunes sync, the stores' copy protection, and the calendar, contacts and photo libraries of the removed apps.

Services of features nothing on this device uses: the set-up helper, device management, VPN and hotspot helpers, search, shared web passwords, asset downloads, usage prediction, storage on camera adapters and the location extras that only apps used.

The helpers the cellular service starts for carrier settings and carrier updates, on an iPad without a cellular radio. The cellular service itself stays, because the Home screen asks for it without pause when it is gone.
The programs those services ran, each used by no launch service that is left.
